title: Fugaro workspace user ls
description: The document `fugaro workspace user ls --json` prints: the workspace's members, what each of them is, and what the workspace knows about their access. It is a named set of fields and not a marshalled workspace.Roster (the `config list` rule): the roster node at `workspaceRosters/<name>` is read by this program and by nothing else, and a consumer reads this document instead. The node's own schema is schemas/workspace-roster.schema.json, and the two are different documents with different readers -- this one carries no folder id, no mechanism detail and no grant the workspace wrote, and every array of it is seeded rather than absent. What an `admin` row says here is the workspace's own admin LIST entry, which is a claim about a binding and not the binding itself: only an entry the live binding backs is trusted (D2823), and `status` is what reports the difference. Members are only ever added within a version, so removing or re-meaning one is what bumps it; no object here is closed for that reason, because a consumer that refused a field this schema does not know would refuse a newer CLI's document of the same version.

version.$comment: workspaceUsersDocVersion in internal/cli/workspace_user.go. 1 is the first version of this document: `workspace user ls` and the schema were published together, so no consumer reads an older one and nothing is owed an explanation yet.

workspace.description: The workspace the flag named, in the spelling the flag carried (a workspace name uses the project-name grammar, config.ProjectNameRE, F21). It is echoed back because a consumer merging two documents -- two workspaces read on one machine, or a document read beside a run's record -- has nothing else in the file that names it.

mechanism.description: How the workspace holds the projects in it (workspace.Mechanisms, D2803): `folder` owns the folder its members' projects are moved into and an admin is a folder owner, `sa` reaches a member through an account of that member's own project. It is here because an admin binding reads differently under the two: a folder owner is read from the folder's IAM, a token creator from the account's.

domains.description: The workspace's allowed domains (D2812), folded and in the order the node holds them. This is the list `fugaro workspace domains` edits, and it is the whole of it: a machine-reader that asked that command for a document would be reading a second contract with a second version. An empty array is a workspace that admits nobody without the external mark, and not a list nobody has read.

members.description: One row per person and machine the workspace's roster holds, in address order (the node's own rule). An empty array is refused by the node's reader rather than written -- a roster names at least one person -- so a consumer that sees one is reading a document from something other than this command.

domain.description: One allowed domain, lower-cased as an address is folded (workspace.CanonicalAddress), and held to the node's own domain grammar by the reader that wrote it.

member.description: One member of the workspace, with what the workspace knows about their access. Nothing here is a credential, and nothing here is a grant the member's own roster has not been asked for: `grants` is read from the members themselves.

address.description: The member's address in its canonical spelling (workspace.CanonicalAddress): a person's email address, or the service account's address a machine is named by. It is what the workspace's roster holds and what the audit trail's subject field carries.

kind.description: Whether the member is a person or a machine (workspace.Kinds, D2806).

external.description: D2812's mark: the person was admitted while their domain was not one of `domains`. It is written on every row, false included, because it is a statement about how somebody was admitted and not a default: the drift check COMPUTES it from `domains` rather than trusting it, so a row whose mark disagrees with the list is a difference that check reports. It is false on every machine, which comes from no domain.

admin.description: The workspace's own admin list names this member. It is a claim about a binding and not the binding: only an entry the live binding backs -- the folder's `roles/owner`, or the workspace IAM account's token creator -- is trusted (D2823), and `fugaro status` is what reports an entry with nothing behind it. It is false on every machine, which is never a workspace admin.

roles.description: A MACHINE's expected per-project roles (D2806): the workspace's record of what it expects the machine to hold, which `status` compares against the live IAM, and not a grant. It is empty on every person, whose roles are grants in the members' own rosters and appear under `grants` instead.

grants.description: The stored grants this member holds in the members' own rosters, one entry per member and per role read there: the member projects in name order, and within one project the order that member's own roster holds. It is empty for a machine, because a member's own roster accepts only `user:` members and a machine is recorded in the workspace alone (D2806). A grant the workspace has written but the member's own `fugaro update` has not applied is not here: what a member holds is read from that member.

role.description: One project a machine is expected to hold a role in.

project.description: The member project the expectation is about, in the workspace's own spelling of it.

role.description: The role the workspace expects the machine to hold there (workspace.Roles).

grant.description: One grant a member holds in one member project's own roster: the role and what it covers. The node it is read from is that member's `config/admin/access` (internal/access), whose scope grammar is D1583: `project` for the whole project, `all-repos` for every repository the published policy admits, or the canonical repository patterns it covers, comma-separated.

project.description: The member project the grant is held in, which is one of the members the workspace links.

role.description: The role granted there, in the member's own roster's vocabulary (internal/access's Role).

scope.description: What the role covers, in the scope grammar the member's roster stores (internal/access's Scope.String): `project`, `all-repos`, or the comma-separated canonical repository patterns of a narrower grant.
